definitions.explanation: The elected head of a city ({市|し}). One of the most common local government titles in Japan. Mayors are directly elected by residents of the city.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{市長|しちょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{就任|しゅうにん}→就任：12368_shuunin⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
{市長|しちょう}{選挙|せんきょ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦{行|おこな}われる→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The mayoral election will be held next month.

examples.japanese: {市長|しちょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{記者|きしゃ}{会見|かいけん}→記者会見：19954_kishakaiken⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{新|あら}た→新た：01697_arata⟧な⟦{防災|ぼうさい}→防災：07907_bousai⟧⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発表|はっぴょう}した→発表する：25231_happyousuru⟧。
examples.english: The mayor announced a new disaster prevention plan at a press conference.

notes:
USAGE:
Japanese local government heads have different titles depending on the type of municipality: {市長|しちょう} (city mayor), ⟦{町長|ちょうちょう}→町長：13580_chouchou⟧ (town mayor), ⟦{村長|そんちょう}→村長：13091_sonchou⟧ (village head), {区長|くちょう} (ward mayor). Together, these are collectively called {首長|しゅちょう} (head of a local government).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {市長|しちょう}{選挙|せんきょ}: mayoral election
- {市長|しちょう}{選|せん}: mayoral race
- {副|ふく}{市長|しちょう}: vice mayor
- {前|ぜん}{市長|しちょう}: former mayor
